entries: A computer is an electronic machine that takes input, processes it according to instructions (a program), stores data and gives output.
What are the parts of a computer?
Main parts: CPU (processor), memory (RAM), storage (hard disk/SSD), motherboard, power supply, and input/output devices like keyboard, mouse and monitor.
The CPU (Central Processing Unit) is the brain of the computer that carries out instructions. It has the ALU (arithmetic logic unit), control unit and registers.
RAM (Random Access Memory) is fast, temporary memory that holds data while the computer is on. It is volatile: it loses its contents when power goes off.
ROM (Read Only Memory) is permanent memory holding start-up instructions; it keeps its data without power (non-volatile).
Hardware is the physical parts of a computer you can touch; software is the programs and instructions that run on it.
An operating system manages the computer's hardware and runs other programs. Examples: Windows, Android, macOS, Linux, iOS.
Input devices send data into a computer: keyboard, mouse, scanner, microphone, webcam, touchscreen.
Output devices show or give results from a computer: monitor, printer, speakers, projector.
What is a bit and a byte?
A bit is a single binary digit (0 or 1). A byte is 8 bits. 1 KB = 1024 bytes, 1 MB = 1024 KB, 1 GB = 1024 MB, 1 TB = 1024 GB.
how many bits in a byte
What is the binary number system?
Binary is a base-2 number system using only 0 and 1, which computers use internally.
The internet is a worldwide network of connected computers that share information using common rules (protocols like TCP/IP).
A web browser is a program for viewing websites, e.g. Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari.
A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is a web address, like https://www.example.com.
HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the language used to build the structure of web pages.
HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is the rule set browsers and servers use to exchange web pages. HTTPS is the secure, encrypted version.
Wi-Fi is wireless networking technology that lets devices connect to a network and the internet using radio waves.
A computer virus is a harmful program that copies itself and spreads to other files or computers, often damaging data. Antivirus software protects against it.
Cloud computing means using storage, software or computing power over the internet instead of on your own device, e.g. Google Drive.
Artificial intelligence (AI) is the ability of computers to do tasks that normally need human intelligence, such as understanding language, recognising images and making decisions.
Machine learning is a part of AI where computers learn patterns from data instead of being told every rule.
An algorithm is a step-by-step set of instructions to solve a problem or do a task.
A programming language is a way of writing instructions for a computer. Examples: Python, JavaScript, Java, C, C++.
A database is an organised collection of data stored so it can be easily searched and updated, e.g. using SQL.
An IP address is a unique number that identifies a device on a network, like 192.168.1.1.
Email (electronic mail) is a way of sending messages over the internet. Ray Tomlinson sent the first network email in 1971.
USB (Universal Serial Bus) is a standard port and cable for connecting devices and charging.
A pixel is the smallest dot of colour on a digital screen or image.
Common shortcuts: Ctrl+C copy, Ctrl+V paste, Ctrl+X cut, Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+Y redo, Ctrl+A select all, Ctrl+S save, Ctrl+P print, Ctrl+F find.
